@@ -111,6 +111,7 @@
-    # Valid characters and a bytes.translate table mapping each character
-    # to its digit value (None if some digit value does not fit in a byte)

+    # Valid characters and a bytes.translate table mapping each character
+    # to its digit value and every invalid character to 255 (None if some
+    # digit value does not fit in a byte below 255)
+    invmap = _get_base58_decode_map(alphabet, autofix=autofix)
+    if max(invmap.values(), default=0) >= 255:
+        return bytes(invmap), None
+    return bytes(invmap), bytes(invmap.get(c, 255) for c in range(256))

+    valid, table = _get_base58_decode_table(alphabet, autofix=autofix)

actions.reason: b58decode_int used to check every input for invalid characters with v.translate(None, valid). Because that call has a delete set, CPython builds a 256-entry translation table on each call before it scans the input. Now the cached digit table sends every character outside the alphabet to 255, so the existing v.translate(table) does the validity check in the same pass, and a single memchr ('255 in digits') finds any bad character. The old deletion scan only runs when a 255 is found, so the error message (first invalid character) stays the same. If an alphabet has a digit value of 255 or more, the table is not used and the old list-based path runs instead. The equivalence harness shows identical outputs. Measured decode_ir ratio 0.9812; check_ir 0.9902; encode_ir unchanged.
